acceptance: internal/core has one nil-safe diagnostics carrier (default os.Stderr) owned by the Orchestrator, set by WithStderr and inherited by cycleRun; ReviewInput.Stderr and leakRecovery.warn are filled from it
The warn io.Writer parameters take the carrier where cycle context exists; dispatchSignalsTo, worktreeAddRetryTo and porcelainDirtySetTo are deleted and their real functions are tested directly
No os.Stderr write remains in non-test internal/core files except the carrier default; a guard test refuses a new one
fix: Add a small diag carrier with a nil-safe Warnf; route the T16 seams through it; migrate the remaining ~187 os.Stderr sites in 3-4 clustered PRs (ship_recovery/continuation_stamp, phase_bindings/decision_branch, rest); land the guard last.
summary: T16 made the stderr output of internal/core injectable with four coexisting patterns (an orchestrator method, struct fields, a warn io.Writer parameter on ~20 functions, and *To wrappers kept for the coverage gate) and moved only the sites that freed a test. One carrier removes the mixed patterns and lets every remaining site and test follow.
title: One diagnostics writer for internal/core, and no raw os.Stderr writes (console part)
